title: OS Command Injection via Shell Interpolation
pattern: Constructing operating system command lines by raw string formatting of unvalidated user inputs and executing them inside a shell interpreter shell sink.
why_bad: The shell interpreter treats control characters (like `;`, `&`, `|`) as statement delimiters, allowing adversaries to append arbitrary shell commands (e.g., `filename = "test.dat; rm -rf /"`) that execute with the application's privileges.
detection: Dynamic string parameters containing variables passed to shell arguments of standard execution commands (e.g. `Command::new("sh").arg("-c")` or `Command::new("bash")`).
fix: Avoid invoking shell interpreters (`sh`, `bash`, `cmd`); invoke process binaries directly, passing arguments as a safe vector/array of independent parameters.
source: `Andrew Hunt & David Thomas - The Pragmatic Programmer (2019)`, p. 63 (Topic 38).
